unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: She is driving to work.
korean: 그녀는 차를 몰고 출근하고 있습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: Please don't make so much noise, I'm trying to work.
korean: 너무 시끄럽게 하지 마세요, 일하는 중이에요.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: Where's Mark? - He's having a shower.
korean: 마크 어디 있나요? - 그는 샤워 중이에요.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: Let's go out now. It isn't raining anymore.
korean: 지금 나가자. 이제 비가 더 이상 안 와.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: Hi Jane, are you enjoying the party?
korean: 안녕 제인, 파티 재미있게 즐기고 있니?

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: What's all that noise? What's going on?
korean: 그 소음은 다 뭐야? 무슨 일이야?

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: I'm reading a really good book at the moment.
korean: 나 요즘 정말 좋은 책을 한 권 읽고 있어.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: Kate wants to work in Italy, so she's learning Italian.
korean: 케이트는 이탈리아에서 일하고 싶어 해서 이탈리아어를 배우고 있어요.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: Some friends of mine are building their own house.
korean: 내 친구 몇 명이 자신들의 집을 직접 짓고 있어.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: They hope to finish it next summer.
korean: 그들은 내년 여름에 완공하기를 희망하고 있어.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: You're working hard today. - Yes, I have a lot to do.
korean: 오늘 열심히 일하시네요. - 네, 할 일이 많아요.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: The company I work for isn't doing so well this year.
korean: 제가 일하는 회사는 올해 실적이 그리 좋지 않습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: Is your English getting better?
korean: 너의 영어 실력이 점점 늘고 있니?

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: The population of the world is increasing very fast.
korean: 세계 인구가 매우 빠르게 증가하고 있습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 1: Daily routines and actions (Present continuous)
english: At first I didn't like my job, but I'm beginning to enjoy it now.
korean: 처음엔 직업이 마음에 안 들었지만, 지금은 점점 좋아지기 시작했어요.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: He drives a bus.
korean: 그는 버스를 운전합니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: Nurses look after patients in hospitals.
korean: 간호사들은 병원에서 환자들을 돌봅니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: I usually go away at weekends.
korean: 저는 보통 주말마다 어딘가로 놀러 갑니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: The earth goes round the sun.
korean: 지구는 태양 주위를 돕니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: The cafe opens at 7:30 in the morning.
korean: 그 카페는 아침 7시 30분에 문을 엽니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: I come from Canada. Where do you come from?
korean: 저는 캐나다 출신입니다. 당신은 어디 출신이신가요?

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: I don't go away very often.
korean: 저는 그리 자주 멀리 떠나지 않습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: What does this word mean?
korean: 이 단어는 무슨 뜻인가요?

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: Rice doesn't grow in cold climates.
korean: 쌀은 추운 기후에서는 자라지 않습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: What do you do? - I work in a shop.
korean: 무슨 일을 하세요? - 저는 가게에서 일합니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: He's always so lazy. He doesn't do anything to help.
korean: 그는 늘 너무 게을러요. 돕기 위해 아무것도 안 해요.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: I get up at 8:00 every morning.
korean: 저는 매일 아침 8시에 일어납니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: How often do you go to the dentist?
korean: 얼마나 자주 치과에 가시나요?

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: Julie doesn't drink tea very often.
korean: 줄리는 차를 그리 자주 마시지 않습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: Robert usually goes away two or three times a year.
korean: 로버트는 보통 일 년에 두세 번 여행을 떠납니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: I promise I won't be late.
korean: 늦지 않겠다고 약속할게요.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: What do you suggest I do? - I suggest that you apologize.
korean: 제가 어떻게 하면 좋을까요? - 사과하시는 것을 제안합니다.

unitTitle: Unit 2: General truths and habits (Present simple)
english: The water is boiling. Can you turn it off?
korean: 물이 끓고 있어요. 불 좀 꺼줄래요?

english: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
korean: 물은 섭씨 100도에서 끓습니다.

english: Listen to those people. What language are they speaking?
korean: 저 사람들의 말을 들어봐. 무슨 언어로 말하고 있는 거지?

english: Excuse me, do you speak English?
korean: 실례합니다, 영어 하실 줄 아나요?

english: Let's go out. It isn't raining now.
korean: 밖에 나가자. 지금은 비가 안 와.

english: It doesn't rain very much in summer.
korean: 여름에는 비가 그리 많이 내리지 않습니다.

english: I'm busy. What are you doing?
korean: 나 바빠. 너 지금 뭐 하고 있어?

english: What do you usually do at weekends?
korean: 주말에는 보통 무엇을 하시나요?

english: I'm getting hungry. Let's go and eat.
korean: 나 배가 고파지고 있어. 가서 밥 먹자.

english: I always get hungry in the afternoon.
korean: 저는 오후가 되면 항상 배가 고파집니다.

english: Most people learn to swim when they are children.
korean: 대부분의 사람들은 어릴 때 수영을 배웁니다.

english: The population of the world is increasing very fast.
korean: 세계 인구는 매우 빠르게 증가하고 있습니다.

english: Every day the population of the world increases by about 200,000 people.
korean: 매일 세계 인구는 약 20만 명씩 증가합니다.

english: I'm living with some friends until I find a place of my own.
korean: 내 집을 구할 때까지 친구 몇 명과 함께 지내고 있어.

english: My parents live in London. They have lived there all their lives.
korean: 저희 부모님은 런던에 사십니다. 평생 그곳에서 사셨어요.

english: You're working hard today. - Yes, I have a lot to do.
korean: 오늘 열심히 일하시네요. - 네, 할 일이 많아요.

english: Joe isn't lazy. He works hard most of the time.
korean: 조는 게으르지 않아요. 대부분의 시간에 열심히 일해요.

english: I always go to work by car.
korean: 저는 항상 차로 출근합니다.

english: I've lost my phone again. I'm always losing things.
korean: 나 또 폰 잃어버렸어. 난 항상 물건을 잃어버린다니까.

english: You're always playing computer games. You should do something more active.
korean: 넌 늘 컴퓨터 게임만 해. 좀 더 활동적인 걸 해봐.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: Tim is never satisfied. He's always complaining.
korean: 팀은 결코 만족하는 법이 없어. 늘 불평만 해.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: I'm hungry. I want something to eat.
korean: 배고파. 뭐 좀 먹을 게 필요해.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: Do you understand what I mean?
korean: 제가 무슨 말을 하는지 이해하시나요?

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: Anna doesn't seem very happy at the moment.
korean: 안나는 지금 그리 행복해 보이지 않아요.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: I think Mary is Canadian, but I'm not sure.
korean: 메리는 캐나다인인 것 같은데, 확실하진 않아요.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: What do you think of my plan?
korean: 내 계획에 대해 어떻게 생각해?

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: I'm thinking about what happened. I often think about it.
korean: 무슨 일이 있었는지 생각하고 있어. 난 종종 그 일을 생각해.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: Nikki is thinking of giving up her job.
korean: 니키는 직장을 그만둘까 고민 중이에요.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: Do you see that man over there?
korean: 저기 서 있는 저 남자 보여요?

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: This room smells. Let's open a window.
korean: 이 방 냄새가 나네. 창문 좀 열자.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: I can hear a strange noise. Can you hear it?
korean: 이상한 소리가 들려. 너도 들리니?

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: You look well today. (or You're looking well today.)
korean: 오늘 안색이 좋아 보여요.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: How do you feel now? (or How are you feeling now?)
korean: 지금 몸 상태는 좀 어떠신가요?

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: I usually feel tired in the morning.
korean: 저는 아침에 보통 피곤함을 느낍니다.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: I can't understand why he's being so selfish. He isn't usually like that.
korean: 그가 왜 저렇게 이기적으로 구는지 이해가 안 돼. 평소엔 안 그러거든.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: He never thinks about other people. He is very selfish.
korean: 그는 남을 배려하지 않아. 정말 이기적이야.

unitTitle: Unit 5: Verbs not used continuously (State verbs)
english: Sarah is very tired. It's hot today.
korean: 사라는 매우 피곤해합니다. 오늘은 날씨가 덥네요.

english: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was an Austrian musician and composer.
korean: 볼프강 아마데우스 모차르트는 오스트리아의 음악가이자 작곡가였습니다.

english: He lived from 1756 to 1791.
korean: 그는 1756년부터 1791년까지 살았습니다.

english: He started composing at the age of five and wrote more than 600 pieces of music.
korean: 그는 5세에 작곡을 시작하여 600곡 이상의 음악을 썼습니다.

english: He was only 35 years old when he died.
korean: 그가 사망했을 때 나이는 겨우 35세였습니다.

english: I work in a travel agency now. Before that, I worked in a department store.
korean: 저는 지금 여행사에서 일합니다. 그 전에는 백화점에서 일했어요.

english: We invited them to our party, but they decided not to come.
korean: 우리는 그들을 파티에 초대했지만, 오지 않기로 결정했습니다.

english: The police stopped me on my way home last night.
korean: 어젯밤 귀가하는 길에 경찰이 나를 멈춰 세웠습니다.

english: Laura passed her exam because she studied very hard.
korean: 로라는 아주 열심히 공부했기 때문에 시험에 합격했습니다.

english: Did you go out last night? - Yes, I went to the cinema, but I didn't enjoy the film much.
korean: 어젯밤 외출했니? - 응, 영화관에 갔는데 영화는 별로 재미없었어.

english: When did Mr. Thomas die? - About 10 years ago.
korean: 토마스 씨는 언제 돌아가셨나요? - 약 10년 전쯤입니다.

english: They didn't invite us to the party, so we didn't go.
korean: 그들이 우리를 파티에 초대하지 않아서 안 갔어요.

english: Did you have time to do the shopping? - No, I didn't.
korean: 쇼핑할 시간 있었니? - 아니, 없었어.

english: What did you do at the weekend? - I didn't do anything.
korean: 주말에 뭐 했어요? - 아무것도 안 했어요.

english: I was angry because they were late.
korean: 그들이 늦어서 화가 났습니다.

english: Was the weather good when you were on holiday?
korean: 휴가 갔을 때 날씨 좋았니?

english: They weren't able to come because they were so busy.
korean: 그들은 너무 바빠서 올 수 없었습니다.

english: Did you go out last night, or were you too tired?
korean: 어젯밤에 외출했니, 아니면 너무 피곤했니?

english: At 10:30 they were playing tennis.
korean: 10시 30분에 그들은 테니스를 치고 있었습니다.

english: This time last year I was living in Brazil.
korean: 작년 이맘때 저는 브라질에 살고 있었습니다.

english: What were you doing at 10:00 last night?
korean: 어젯밤 10시에 뭐 하고 계셨나요?

english: I waved to Helen, but she wasn't looking.
korean: 헬렌에게 손을 흔들었지만, 그녀는 보고 있지 않았습니다.

english: I was walking home when I met Dan.
korean: 집으로 걸어가던 중에 댄을 만났습니다.

english: I walked home after the party last night.
korean: 어젯밤 파티가 끝난 후 나는 집까지 걸어갔습니다.

english: Kate was watching TV when we arrived.
korean: 우리가 도착했을 때 케이트는 TV를 보고 있었습니다.

english: Kate watched TV a lot when she was ill last year.
korean: 케이트는 작년에 아팠을 때 TV를 많이 보았습니다.

english: Matt phoned while we were having dinner.
korean: 우리가 저녁을 먹고 있을 때 매트가 전화를 걸었습니다.

english: It was raining when I got up.
korean: 내가 일어났을 때 비가 내리고 있었습니다.

english: I saw you in the park yesterday. You were sitting on the grass and reading a book.
korean: 어제 공원에서 널 봤어. 잔디밭에 앉아서 책을 읽고 있더라.

english: I hurt my back while I was working in the garden.
korean: 정원에서 일하다가 허리를 다쳤습니다.

english: I was walking along the road when I saw Dan, so I stopped and we had a chat.
korean: 길을 걷다가 댄을 봐서 멈춰 서서 이야기를 나눴습니다.

english: When Karen arrived, we were having dinner.
korean: 카렌이 도착했을 때 우리는 저녁을 먹고 있었습니다.

english: When Karen arrived, we had dinner.
korean: 카렌이 도착하자 우리는 저녁을 먹었습니다.

english: We were good friends. We knew each other well.
korean: 우리는 좋은 친구였습니다. 우리는 서로를 잘 알고 있었죠.

english: I was enjoying the party, but Chris wanted to go home.
korean: 나는 파티가 즐거웠지만, 크리스는 집에 가고 싶어 했습니다.
